arxiv-1707-01462.title: Automorphisms of 𝑷 𝟏 \boldsymbol{\mathbb{P}^{1}}\! -bundles over rational surfaces
arxiv-1707-01462.creator: Jérémy Blanc, Andrea Fanelli, Ronan Terpereau
arxiv-1707-01462.description: Abstract Abstract. In this paper, we provide the complete classification of \mathbb{P}^{1}\! -bundles over smooth projective rational surfaces whose neutral component of the automorphism group is maximal. Our results hold over any algebraically closed field of characteristic zero. Keywords. Rational threefolds, vector bundles, \mathbb{P}^{1}\! -bundles, automorphisms, birational maps, algebraic groups, classification 2020 Mathematics Subject Classification.

arxiv-1709-00597.title: Troisième groupe de cohomologie non ramifiée d’un solide cubique sur un corps de fonctions d’une variable
arxiv-1709-00597.creator: Jean-Louis Colliot-Thélène et Alena Pirutka
arxiv-1709-00597.description: Abstract Résumé En combinant une méthode de C. Voisin avec la descente galoisienne sur le groupe de Chow en codimension 2 2 , nous montrons que le troisième groupe de cohomologie non ramifiée d’un solide cubique lisse défini sur le corps des fonctions d’une courbe complexe est nul.

arxiv-1904-00705.title: MPP-2019-39 A prescription for projectors to compute helicity amplitudes in D dimensions
arxiv-1904-00705.creator: Long Chen
arxiv-1904-00705.description: Abstract This article discusses a prescription to compute polarized dimensionally regularized amplitudes, providing a recipe for constructing simple and general polarized amplitude projectors in D dimensions that avoids conventional Lorentz tensor decomposition and avoids also dimensional splitting. Because of the latter, commutation between Lorentz index contraction and loop integration is preserved within this prescription, which entails certain technical advantages.

arxiv-2102-10093.title: Almost everywhere balanced sequences of complexity 2 ​ n + 1 2n+1
arxiv-2102-10093.creator: Julien Cassaigne, Sébastien Labbé, Julien Leroy
arxiv-2102-10093.description: Abstract . We study ternary sequences associated with a multidimensional continued fraction algorithm introduced by the first author. The algorithm is defined by two matrices and we show that it is measurably isomorphic to the shift on the set { 1 , 2 } ℕ \{1,2\}^{\mathbb{N}} of directive sequences.

arxiv-2205-04922.title: On the stabilizing effect of swimming in an active suspension
arxiv-2205-04922.creator: Dallas Albritton, Laurel Ohm
arxiv-2205-04922.description: Abstract We consider a kinetic model of an active suspension of rod-like microswimmers. In certain regimes, swimming has a stabilizing effect on the suspension. We quantify this effect near homogeneous isotropic equilibria ψ ¯ = const \overline{\psi}=\text{const} . Notably, in the absence of particle (translational and orientational) diffusion, swimming is the only stabilizing mechanism.

arxiv-2212-00045.title: Probing the Mechanism of Neutrinoless Double-Beta Decay in Multiple Isotopes
arxiv-2212-00045.creator: Matteo Agostini, Frank F. Deppisch, Graham Van Goffrier
arxiv-2212-00045.description: Abstract A large experimental program is being mounted to search for neutrinoless double-beta decay over the next decade. Multiple experiments using different target isotopes are being prepared to explore the whole parameter space allowed for inverted-ordered light neutrinos, and have the potential to make discoveries in several other scenarios, including normal-ordered light neutrinos and other exotic mechanisms.

arxiv-2305-02705.title: Guidance & Control Networks for Time-Optimal Quadcopter Flight
arxiv-2305-02705.creator: Sebastien Origer, Christophe De Wagter, Robin Ferede, Guido C.H.E. de Croon, Dario Izzo
arxiv-2305-02705.description: Abstract Reaching fast and autonomous flight requires computationally efficient and robust algorithms. To this end, we train Guidance & Control Networks to approximate optimal control policies ranging from energy-optimal to time-optimal flight. We show that the policies become more difficult to learn the closer we get to the time-optimal ’bang-bang’ control profile.

arxiv-2402-00093.title: ChIRAAG: ChatGPT Informed Rapid and Automated Assertion Generation
arxiv-2402-00093.creator: Bhabesh Mali*, Karthik Maddala*, Vatsal Gupta*, Sweeya Reddy*, Chandan Karfa*, Ramesh Karri†
arxiv-2402-00093.description: Abstract System Verilog Assertion (SVA) formulation- a critical yet complex task is a prerequisite in the Assertion Based Verification (ABV) process . Traditionally, SVA formulation involves expert-driven interpretation of specifications, which is time-consuming and prone to human error. Recently, LLM-informed automatic assertion generation is gaining interest.

arxiv-2402-10889.description: Abstract The fifth generation of the telecommunication networks (5G) established the service-oriented paradigm on the mobile networks. In this new context, the 5G Core component has become extremely flexible so, in addition to serving mobile networks, it can also be used to connect devices from the so-called non-3GPP networks, which contains technologies such as WiFi.

arxiv-2511-00416.title: PADBen: A Comprehensive Benchmark for Evaluating AI Text Detectors Against Paraphrase Attacks
arxiv-2511-00416.creator: Yiwei Zha, Rui Min, Sushmita Shanu
arxiv-2511-00416.description: A 2025 arXiv research paper by Yiwei Zha, Rui Min, Sushmita Shanu. While AI-generated text (AIGT) detectors achieve over 90% accuracy on direct LLM outputs, they fail catastrophically against iteratively-paraphrased content. We investigate why iteratively-paraphrased text—itself AI-generated—evades detection systems designed for AIGT identification. Through intrinsic mechanism analysis, we reveal that iterative paraphrasing creates an intermediate laundering region characterized by semantic displacement with preserved generation patterns, which brings up two attack categories: paraphrasing human-authored text (authorship obfuscation) and paraphrasing LLM-generated text (plagiarism evasion).

arxiv-2511-18329.title: SciPostLayoutTree: A Dataset for Structural Analysis of Scientific Posters
arxiv-2511-18329.creator: Shohei Tanaka, Atsushi Hashimoto, Yoshitaka Ushiku
arxiv-2511-18329.description: Abstract Scientific posters play a vital role in academic communication by presenting ideas through visual summaries. Analyzing reading order and parent-child relations of posters is essential for building structure-aware interfaces that facilitate clear and accurate understanding of research content. Despite their prevalence in academic communication, posters remain underexplored in structural analysis research, which has primarily focused on papers.

arxiv-2601-04889.title: Faithful Summarisation under Disagreement via Belief-Level Aggregation
arxiv-2601-04889.creator: Favour Yahdii Aghaebe, Tanefa Apekey, Elizabeth Williams, Nafise Sadat Moosavi
arxiv-2601-04889.description: Abstract Opinion and multi-document summarisation often involve genuinely conflicting viewpoints, yet many existing approaches, particularly LLM-based systems, implicitly smooth disagreement and over-represent majority opinions. This limits the faithfulness of generated summaries in opinion-heavy settings. We introduce a disagreement-aware synthesis pipeline that separates belief-level aggregation from language generation.

pmc-10600585.title: Antiplatelet Therapy in Patients With Abdominal Aortic Aneurysm Without Symptomatic Atherosclerotic Disease
pmc-10600585.creator: Chalotte W. Nicolajsen, Mette Søgaard, Martin Jensen, Nikolaj Eldrup, Torben B. Larsen, Samuel Z. Goldhaber, Christian-Alexander Behrendt, Peter B. Nielsen
pmc-10600585.description: Key PointsQuestionDo patients with abdominal aortic aneurysms without symptomatic atherosclerosis benefit from antiplatelet therapy?FindingsIn this comparative effectiveness research study using target trial emulation methods including 6344 patients with 131 047 trial cases, limited effectiveness of antiplatelets to lower the risk of ischemic events was noted. The absolute risk differences between the treatment groups were minimal.

pmc-11480951.title: Recommendations for Designing, Conducting, and Reporting Feeding Trials in Nutrition Research
pmc-11480951.creator: Delyse SY Tien, Meghan Hockey, Daniel So, Jordan Stanford, Erin D Clarke, Clare E Collins, Heidi M Staudacher
pmc-11480951.description: Double-blind, placebo-controlled, randomized controlled trials are the gold standard for clinical trials in nutrition science. For trials of whole diets, dietary counseling is advantageous as they offer clinical translatability although can vary in the fidelity of the intended intervention from participant to participant and across studies.

pmc-11488357.title: Individual empowerment and community norm effects of engaging young husbands in reproductive health in rural India: findings from a pilot study
pmc-11488357.creator: Nadia Diamond-Smith, Yogesh Vaishnav, Usha Choudhary, Payal Sharma, Ankur Kachhwaha, Tamera Panjalingam, Janelli Vallin, Debangana Das, Lakshmi Gopalakrishnan
pmc-11488357.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2024). BackgroundDespite decades of a call to action to engage men in reproductive health, men are often left out of programs and interventions. In India, where half of pregnancies are reported as unintended, patriarchal gender norms and still dominant patterns of arranged marriages make engaging men in family planning and strengthening couples communication critical in increasing reproductive autonomy and helping young couples meet their reproductive goals.

pmc-11505186.title: Implementing an Antimicrobial Stewardship Lecture Series for Family Medicine Residency Programs in South Carolina
pmc-11505186.creator: Kayla Antosz, Pamela Bailey, Majdi Al-Hasan, Brandon Bookstaver, Hana Winders, Sarah Battle
pmc-11505186.description: Background: Family medicine physicians are one of the leading prescribers of antimicrobials in both the inpatient and ambulatory setting, however appropriate education on antimicrobial stewardship (AS) is lacking. The Antimicrobial Stewardship Collaborative of South Carolina (ASC-SC) created a family medicine AS lecture series to increase awareness of stewardship, improve antimicrobial prescribing throughout the state, and ultimately combat antimicrobial resistance.

pmc-11603044.title: An autonomous navigation system with a trajectory prediction-based decision mechanism for rubber forest navigation
pmc-11603044.creator: Xirui Zhang, Yongqi Liu, Junxiao Liu, Xuanli Chen, Ruiwu Xu, Weiqiang Ma, Zhifu Zhang, Shaohua Fu
pmc-11603044.description: The use of rubber-tapping robots capable of autonomous navigation in place of manual rubber-tapping is a growing trend, but the challenging multi-objective navigation task in forest environments impedes their autonomous operation. To tackle this issue, an autonomous navigation system with a trajectory prediction-based decision mechanism for rubber forest navigation is designed.

pmc-11717349.title: Peer coaching in cardiac surgery: a pilot study on rehabilitation participation and perioperative challenges
pmc-11717349.creator: Kanwar Parhar, Aaron Holm, Ravi S Hira, Lara Oyetunji, Jeannie Collins-Brandon, Eric J Lehr, Sarah Speck
pmc-11717349.description: Following cardiac surgery, active participation in cardiac rehabilitation (CR) is associated with reduced cardiovascular events and improved survival. However, CR attendance remains persistently low, with only ∼25% of patients participating. The Peer Coaching for Cardiac Patients (PCCP) pilot programme aimed to assess whether peer coaching could enhance CR participation and reduce perioperative anxiety and depression in cardiac surgery patients.

pmc-12559801.title: Beyond body mass index: the role of fat distribution in male sperm quality
pmc-12559801.creator: Dongsheng Ma, Mengru Zhang, Xiaoguang Zhang, Lizhen Xu
pmc-12559801.description: ObjectiveTo explore the dual role of obesity and fat distribution on sperm dynamics and morphological parameters and to further assess the impact on male fertility.MethodsA population of 823 male semen examinations from the Male Reproductive Health Database (FAST-Date, 2022-2025), was retrospectively analyzed for general information, obesity indicators, sperm dynamics and morphology parameter ratings, and male fertility assessment indicators.

pmc-12857152.description: IntroductionThe training of clinical specialists in Malaysia on completion of the undergraduate medical programme is long and expansive. pmc-12885151.title: Recent trends in sales of electronic nicotine devices and oral nicotine pouches by flavour
pmc-12885151.creator: Clinton H Durney, Rafael Meza, Evelyn Jimenez-Mendoza, Ke Xu, David T Levy, Abigail S Friedman
pmc-12885151.description: BackgroundThe landscape of tobacco and nicotine delivery products has rapidly evolved with the introduction of electronic nicotine delivery systems (ENDSs) and oral nicotine pouches (ONPs). Understanding sales trends and flavour preferences is critical for assessing these products’ public health impact and informing regulatory strategies.

pmc-13068818.title: OGG1 increases exercise endurance via elevated skeletal muscle FGF21
pmc-13068818.creator: Bhavya Blaze, Priyanka Sharma, Bhavya Prakash Gupta, Souvik Mandal, Sai Santosh Babu Komakula, Tracy Anthony, Emmanuel Marfo, Harini Sampath
pmc-13068818.description: The base excision repair pathway maintains genomic integrity in the face of oxidative insult. It is initiated by DNA glycosylases such as 8-oxoguanine DNA glycosylase (OGG1) and is implicated in various pathologies, such as cancers and neurodegenerative diseases. Base excision repair proteins also modulate body weight and metabolic health.

pmc-13076479.title: Effects of a culturally tailored intervention on medication adherence in Chinese and Vietnamese Americans with hepatitis B: a randomized controlled trial
pmc-13076479.creator: Lin Zhu, Wenyue Lu, Zhiqing Elaine Liu, Di Zhu, Ming-Chin Yeh, Minhhuyen T. Nguyen, Yin Tan, Min Qi Wang, Grace X. Ma
pmc-13076479.description: IntroductionAsian Americans are disproportionately affected by chronic hepatitis B (CHB), which is caused by infection with hepatitis B virus (HBV). While adherence to antiviral medication is an effective practical approach to managing CHB and preventing liver cancer, medication adherence rates among Chinese and Vietnamese Americans with CHB, two vulnerable yet understudied populations, remain largely unknown.

pmc-13224038.title: A digitally embedded intervention to enhance psychological decentering and reduce depression severity in at-risk adolescents: a randomised controlled trial of the ‘One Step Back’ programme
pmc-13224038.creator: Rachel Knight, Hannah Clegg, Edwin S Dalmaijer, Darren Dunning, Grace Franckel, Bert Lenaert, Anna Sakol, Timothy R Sandhu, Maris Vainre, Peter Watson, Gem Wright, The MYRIAD Team, Tamsin Ford, Willem Kuyken, Sarah-Jayne Blakemore, Tim Dalgleish, Marc Bennett
pmc-13224038.description: SummaryBackgroundAdolescence is a critical period for early mental health interventions. Scalable, evidence-based interventions for at-risk adolescents without severe symptoms are limited. We developed a low-intensity, digital programme to train psychological decentering (the ability to disengage from unwanted thoughts, feelings, and memories) as a core psychotherapeutic process for improving mental health.

pmc-13523377.creator: Yu-Seok Kim, Seung Jin Yoo, Sung-San Park, Jong-Hun Kim, Jae Chul Yoo
pmc-13523377.description: BackgroundReverse total shoulder arthroplasty (RTSA) is a well-established replacement strategy to treat irreparable massive rotator cuff tears and cuff tear arthropathy. In patients with forward (FF) deficits combined with a loss of external rotation (ER), RSA with latissimus dorsi transfer (LDT), which was initially used for brachial plexopathies, has been addressed to restore both functional deficits.

pmc-13679289.title: Meningioma in the modern era: Updates in stratification and therapeutic approaches
pmc-13679289.creator: Leeor S. Yefet, Gelareh Zadeh, Farshad Nassiri
pmc-13679289.description: Meningioma is the most common primary intracranial tumor in adults. Most meningiomas have an indolent growth pattern, but some can grow quickly. The World Health Organization (WHO) classification system is the gold standard for tumor grading and relies predominantly on histopathology and limited molecular alterations.

pmc-13717466.title: Implementing trust in non-small cell lung cancer diagnosis with a conformalized uncertainty-aware AI framework
pmc-13717466.creator: Xiaoge Zhang, Tao Wang, Chao Yan, Fedaa Najdawi, Kai Zhou, Yuan Ma, Yiu-ming Cheung, Maximus C. F. Yeung, Bradley A. Malin
pmc-13717466.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). Ensuring trustworthiness is fundamental in cancer diagnostics, where a misdiagnosis can have dire consequences. Current pathology AI models lack systematic solutions to address trustworthiness concerns arising from model limitations and data discrepancies between model deployment and development environments. Here we introduce TRUECAM (Trustworthiness-focused, Uncertainty-aware, End-to-end Cancer diagnosis with Model-agnostic capabilities), a framework designed to ensure both data and model trustworthiness for non-small cell lung cancer subtyping with whole-slide images.
